eligibility.text: An individual registering a trading name for a business they own. Governed by the Business Names Act, 1962 (Act 151).
To create an account on the ORC portal you need a TIN, or a scanned government-issued photo ID such as the Ghana Card, passport, voter's ID or driver's licence.
Since April 2021 the PIN on your Ghana Card serves as your TIN, so for most individuals the Ghana Card is what you need.

steps.action: Search whether your chosen business name is available, and reserve it if you wish
steps.note: A name search costs GH¢30.00. A reserved name is held while you complete the registration.

steps.action: Create a user account on the ORC online portal - this is free
Download, print, complete, sign and scan Form A
Open Entity Registration on the portal and choose to create a new entity, or to use a name you already reserved
Complete every field on the application and upload your signed, scanned Form A
Pay online through the Ghana Electronic Payment Platform - VISA, Mastercard, eTransact, mobile money or bank transfer
Wait for the SMS telling you the status of your application
Download your electronic certificate and related documents within 14 days
steps.note: After 14 days each document costs GH¢10.00 to re-issue. Certified hard copies are collected at the ORC office for the region you selected.

Annual renewal of a business name

timeline.expedited: 24 hours through the ORC Prestige Centre
timeline.note: ORC does not publish a standard processing time. It tells you the status by SMS. Only the expedited Prestige service has a published turnaround.

rejection_causes.text: Leaving fields blank on the application - ORC's own guide warns against this explicitly.
Choosing a name that is already taken. Running the paid name search first avoids this.

caveats.text: ORC fees changed on 2 February 2026. Guides and blog posts published before that date quote superseded amounts.

The document and step details come from an official Government of Ghana pamphlet that carries no date, so it may not reflect practice after the February 2026 changes. ORC's own service pages could not be read automatically.

At least one director must be resident in Ghana at all times.
You need at least one shareholder.
Every officer - director, secretary and shareholder - needs an individual TIN, which for individuals is the Ghana Card PIN.
You need a signed letter of consent from an auditor before you apply.
The company name must end with the word LIMITED.

eligibility.text: Individuals with taxable income, including employees, self-employed people and professionals, must be registered for tax.
All businesses must be registered - sole proprietorships, partnerships and companies.
Since 1 April 2021 the Ghana Card PIN replaced the TIN for individuals. GRA states plainly that the PIN on your Ghana Card is now your TIN.
GRA continues to generate and issue a TIN to organisations, companies and other legal persons.

name: VAT Registration
summary: Registering to charge Value Added Tax under the Value Added Tax Act, 2025 (Act 1151), which took effect on 1 January 2026.
aliases: how do I register for VAT
GRA VAT registration

VAT number for my company

eligibility.text: If you supply taxable SERVICES there is no threshold at all - you must register. GRA has clarified publicly that the GH¢750,000 threshold applies only to goods.
If you supply GOODS you must register once taxable supplies exceed GH¢750,000 in any twelve-month period, or where there is reasonable ground to expect they will exceed it in the next twelve months.
You must also register where supplies exceed GH¢187,500 in a three-month period and total supplies for that quarter plus the following nine months are expected to exceed GH¢750,000.
You must apply within 30 days of engaging in the taxable activity, or within 30 days of meeting the goods threshold.
The VAT Flat Rate Scheme has been abolished. If you were registered under it you must charge the standard rate until GRA formally deregisters or migrates you, and return unused flat rate booklets.

Certificate of incorporation or business registration certificate
documents.where_to_obtain: Office of the Registrar of Companies

documents.name: Ghana Card of the owner or directors

Financial statements

steps.action: Make sure you have a Ghana Card and, for a business, an ORC registration certificate
Register as a taxpayer - online with your Ghana Card PIN, or in person at a Taxpayer Service Centre
steps.location: taxpayersportal.com or a GRA Taxpayer Service Centre

steps.action: Apply specifically for the VAT tax type at a Taxpayer Service Centre
steps.note: GRA directs VAT tax-type registration to a service centre; the online portal is for filing and payment.

steps.action: Receive your VAT registration and certificate from GRA
Sign up on the taxpayers' portal - free, one account per TIN
Begin charging VAT and file monthly returns by the last working day of the following month

fees.label: VAT registration
fees.note: GRA publishes no registration fee. Signing up on the taxpayers' portal is expressly free. Confirm at a Taxpayer Service Centre.

fees.label: VAT rate charged after registration
fees.amount_text: 15% VAT plus 2.5% NHIL and 2.5% GETFund Levy - 20% in total
fees.note: The COVID-19 Health Recovery Levy is abolished. NHIL and GETFund are now claimable as input tax credits.

fees.label: Penalty for failing to register
fees.amount_text: Not less than three times the tax on the taxable supplies, from the date registration was required

timeline.note: GRA publishes no processing time for VAT registration. What is fixed is your deadline to apply: 30 days.

rejection_causes.text: Assuming the GH¢750,000 threshold protects a service business. It does not - services have no threshold.
Continuing to charge the old flat rate after Act 1151 took effect, instead of the standard rate.

caveats.text: GRA's own VAT web page describes the threshold change without clearly separating goods from services. The goods-only reading comes from GRA officials' public clarification in January 2026. If you supply services, do not assume a threshold protects you.
The statutory detail here comes from a reproduction of Act 1151, not from a GRA-hosted readable copy. GRA's own VAT Guidelines PDF is the document to check before you act.

eligibility.text: Any business, company, organisation or entity in Ghana that employs one or more workers must register with SSNIT.
As an employer you must ensure all employees are registered under the scheme and make regular contributions on their behalf.

steps.action: Assemble the documents listed above
Visit the nearest SSNIT branch with the documents
steps.note: An employer enrolment page exists at portal.ssnit.org.gh/employer/enroll, but SSNIT does not confirm whether registration can be completed entirely online.

steps.action: SSNIT approves your registration and issues a unique Employer Registration (ER) number
Enrol each employee as a member using Form iSS1A so every worker has a social security number
Deduct 5.5% from each worker's salary, add 13% of basic salary, and remit 13.5% to SSNIT within 14 days of the following month
Submit a contribution report by the end of every month, even if you have not yet remitted the funds
Arrange the Tier 2 scheme with a licensed corporate trustee - the remaining 5% does not go to SSNIT
steps.location: A licensed corporate trustee regulated by NPRA

fees.label: Employer registration fee
fees.note: SSNIT publishes no registration fee on its website. That does not mean it is free - it means it is unpublished. Ask at the branch.

fees.label: Employee deduction
fees.amount_text: 5.5% of the worker's salary each month

fees.label: Employer contribution
fees.note: Employee and employer together make 18.5%. Of that, 13.5% goes to SSNIT (Tier 1) and 5% to the Tier 2 scheme.

fees.label: Penalty for unpaid contributions
fees.amount_text: 3% per month on the unpaid amount, with a further 3% per month if you fail to pay after a written demand

timeline.note: SSNIT says the ER number is issued on approval but publishes no turnaround time. What is fixed is your deadline: remit within 14 days of the following month.

rejection_causes.text: An incomplete document set - most often the Assembly's local authority certificate, the certificate to commence business, or a missing sector certificate.

caveats.text: The 5% Tier 2 contribution does not go to SSNIT. You arrange that separately with a licensed corporate trustee regulated by the National Pensions Regulatory Authority.

eligibility.text: Every person or entity operating a profession, occupation, trade or business within an Assembly's area must hold a permit. This is required by law regardless of your size or turnover.
It covers artisans and the self-employed too - mechanics, electricians, plumbers, tailors, hairdressers - not only registered companies.
The permit expires on 31 December of the year it is issued, whatever month you got it. Businesses starting after January pay a pro-rata rate.

fees.label: Penalty for operating without a permit
fees.amount_text: A fine of 100 to 250 penalty units, or 30 days to 6 months imprisonment, or both, with additional daily fines for a continuing offence

timeline.note: AMA does not publish a maximum time to the permanent permit.

rejection_causes.text: Incorrect business classification, which leads to a wrong fee assessment. AMA has publicly urged owners to give the Assembly the information needed to classify their business correctly.
Arrears on previous permits or property rates.

caveats.text: This card is written from Accra Metropolitan Assembly's published process. Every Assembly differs in documents, fees and process. Treat it as the shape of the process, then confirm with your own Assembly.

Some sources list tax clearance, fire and environmental health certificates as required. AMA's own page does not list them, though regulated activities such as food service or fuel do need sector clearances in practice.

eligibility.text: You need a permit to erect any building or structure, to make structural alterations or renovations, to install fittings connected to structures, or to carry out engineering or mining operations on land.
You must hold and be able to show an interest in the land, and your proposal must match the zoning of the area.
A permit lasts five years from issue. Temporary structure permits are renewable every six months up to a maximum of five years.

steps.action: Submit the application at the Assembly secretariat and pay the submission and processing fees
The Physical Planning Department vets it for zoning and planning compliance, alongside the Works Department and other agencies
Technical findings are collated
A Physical Planning Officer and a Works Engineer inspect the site
The Technical Sub-Committee assesses and makes recommendations
The Statutory Planning Committee decides - approval, refusal, or queries and deferment
You are notified, the permit is prepared and permit fees are assessed
Pay the permit fee and receive your development or building permit

fees.label: Processing and permit fees
fees.note: Fees are assessed on floor area, use class and development value, set by each Assembly's annual fee-fixing resolution. There is no national figure. Processing fees are due at submission and permit fees on approval.

timeline.standard: The Statutory Planning Committee must decide within 30 working days of submission; you are notified within 3 working days of the meeting and the written permit is issued within 14 days of the decision
timeline.note: The 30-working-day period comes from Regulation 44(10) of L.I. 2384. No published consequence exists if the authority misses it.

rejection_causes.text: The proposal does not conform to the zoning status of the area.
Required documentation is missing or incomplete.
Adverse findings at the site inspection.

caveats.text: Written from Accra Metropolitan Assembly's published checklist. Requirements and fees differ by Assembly.

A deferment for queries is not the same as a refusal, and it is common. If you are refused, you have up to six months to appeal - AMA describes the appeal as going to the Regional Coordinating Council while LUSPA's guidelines say the Regional Minister. Confirm the route with your Assembly.

summary: Ghana's official national digital addressing system. Every 5m by 5m square in the country already has a permanent address - you read yours off the app rather than applying for it.

eligibility.text: Open to anyone. There is no application and no approval - the system already covers every inch of the country in 5m by 5m squares, each with a permanent unique address.
You need a smartphone with location enabled, or access to the web map.

documents.name: No documents are needed
documents.note: The app asks you to register and verify with your details, but nothing has to be produced or proved.

steps.action: Download the GhanaPostGPS app free from Google Play or the App Store
Install it and complete registration and verification
Turn on your phone's location
Stand in front of or inside the property you want the address for - accuracy depends on where you physically stand
Open the app and tap the location button; your digital address appears
Check the accuracy colour: green means 3-9m and is best, yellow 10-20m is acceptable, red is above 20m and you should move or wait for a better signal
Save or share the code. The format is a region and district prefix, an area code and a unique identifier - for example AK-039-5028 is Kumasi Main Post Office

fees.label: Digital address
fees.note: No payment is required to download or use the app. Standard mobile data charges apply for the web map.

timeline.standard: Instant - the address is generated in real time as soon as your location is acquired

rejection_causes.text: There is no application to reject. The common failures are practical: location services switched off, poor GPS accuracy showing red, or not standing at the property itself - which gives you the address of the wrong square.

caveats.text: We did not find a route for people without a smartphone - no USSD code or Ghana Post counter service is published. If you have no smartphone, someone else can generate the address while standing at your property.
